name: Unclear Navigation
description: Users have difficulty understanding where they are, where they can go, or how to reach the content or function they need. This issue often appears when menu labels are vague, navigation paths are inconsistent, or important sections are hidden behind unclear categories.
aliases: confusing navigation| poor wayfinding| hidden routes| unclear menu
examples: I could not find where to change my account settings.

name: Poor Information Architecture
description: Content, pages, actions, or features are organized in a way that does not match users’ expectations or mental models. Users may understand the interface elements individually but still struggle because the overall structure feels illogical or fragmented.
aliases: bad structure| confusing organization| misplaced content| poor grouping
examples: The refund policy was under Help, but I expected it under Orders.

name: Ambiguous Labels
description: Buttons, links, headings, form fields, or menu items use wording that is too vague, technical, or misleading. Users cannot confidently predict what will happen when they interact with the element.
aliases: unclear wording| vague labels| confusing copy| misleading label
examples: I was not sure whether Continue would save my changes or skip the step.

name: Hidden Primary Action
description: The main action users need to complete a task is difficult to notice, visually weak, or placed somewhere unexpected. This reduces task efficiency and may cause users to abandon the flow.
aliases: buried CTA| invisible action| hard-to-find button| weak primary action
examples: I wanted to submit the form, but the button was hidden at the bottom.

name: Inconsistent Interaction Patterns
description: The interface behaves differently across similar pages, components, or workflows. Users must relearn interactions because buttons, menus, icons, gestures, or layouts do not work consistently.
aliases: inconsistent UI| unpredictable behavior| pattern mismatch| interaction inconsistency
examples: Sometimes clicking the card opens details, but other times it selects the item.

name: Missing Feedback
description: The system does not clearly confirm that an action has been received, completed, failed, or is still processing. Users are left uncertain about the state of the system.
aliases: no feedback| silent action| missing confirmation| unclear response
examples: After I clicked Save, nothing happened, so I clicked it again.

name: Slow System Response
description: Pages, actions, searches, uploads, or transitions take longer than expected, interrupting the user's flow and increasing frustration. This is especially problematic when there is no loading state or explanation.
aliases: slow performance| lag| delay| long loading
examples: The page took several seconds to update after I applied the filter.

name: Poor Error Prevention
description: The interface allows users to make avoidable mistakes instead of guiding them before the error occurs. This includes weak validation, dangerous defaults, confusing controls, or missing constraints.
aliases: avoidable error| weak validation| unsafe default| preventable mistake
examples: I submitted the form before realizing I had selected the wrong date.

name: Unhelpful Error Message
description: An error message appears but does not explain what went wrong, where the issue is, or how the user can fix it. The message may be too generic, technical, or blame the user.
aliases: vague error| technical error| unclear failure| bad error copy
examples: It just said Invalid input, but it did not tell me which field was wrong.

name: Error Recovery Friction
description: After an error occurs, users have difficulty correcting it or returning to a safe state. They may lose entered data, be forced to restart, or receive no path to resolve the problem.
aliases: hard recovery| dead end error| lost progress| restart required
examples: When payment failed, I had to fill in the entire checkout form again.

name: Excessive Cognitive Load
description: The interface presents too much information, too many decisions, or too many competing elements at once. Users must work harder than necessary to understand what matters and what to do next.
aliases: mental overload| clutter| too many options| high effort
examples: There were so many settings on the page that I did not know where to start.

name: Visual Clutter
description: The screen is visually overloaded with dense content, decorative elements, excessive borders, competing colors, or poor spacing. This makes scanning and prioritization difficult.
aliases: busy layout| cluttered screen| crowded UI| noisy design
examples: The dashboard had so many cards and icons that I could not tell what was important.

name: Poor Visual Hierarchy
description: Important information or actions are not visually emphasized enough, while less important elements receive too much attention. Users struggle to scan the page and identify priority.
aliases: weak hierarchy| poor emphasis| unclear priority| flat layout
examples: The delete button was more noticeable than the button to complete the task.

name: Low Readability
description: Text is difficult to read because of small font size, poor contrast, dense paragraphs, awkward line length, or overly complex language. This affects comprehension, speed, and comfort.
aliases: hard to read| dense text| poor legibility| text overload
examples: The instructions were written in long paragraphs and I had to reread them.

name: Poor Accessibility Contrast
description: Text, icons, controls, or states do not have enough contrast against their background. Users with low vision, color vision deficiencies, or situational limitations may struggle to perceive content.
aliases: low contrast| inaccessible colors| weak visibility| color contrast issue
examples: The gray text on the white background was almost impossible to read.

name: Keyboard Navigation Issue
description: Users cannot efficiently navigate or operate the interface using only a keyboard. Focus order may be illogical, focus indicators may be missing, or important controls may be unreachable.
aliases: keyboard trap| poor tab order| missing focus| keyboard inaccessible
examples: I tabbed through the page but could not reach the dropdown menu.

name: Screen Reader Accessibility Issue
description: The interface does not provide meaningful structure, labels, roles, or announcements for assistive technologies. Screen reader users may miss content, misunderstand controls, or lose context.
aliases: screen reader issue| missing ARIA| unlabeled control| inaccessible markup
examples: The screen reader announced the button as button but did not say what it did.

name: Color-Only Communication
description: The interface relies only on color to communicate status, priority, selection, warnings, or errors. Users who cannot distinguish the colors may miss important information.
aliases: color dependency| color-only status| inaccessible state| no non-color cue
examples: The only difference between available and unavailable dates was the color.

name: Small Touch Target
description: Clickable or tappable elements are too small or too close together, making them difficult to select accurately, especially on mobile or touch devices.
aliases: tiny button| hard to tap| small hit area| cramped controls
examples: I kept tapping the wrong icon because the buttons were too close together.

name: Poor Mobile Responsiveness
description: The interface does not adapt well to smaller screens. Content may overflow, controls may become cramped, important actions may disappear, or layouts may require excessive scrolling.
aliases: bad mobile layout| responsive issue| mobile friction| broken small screen
examples: On my phone, the table was cut off and I could not see the action buttons.

name: Form Complexity
description: Forms require too much effort because they contain unnecessary fields, unclear grouping, poor defaults, repeated information, or too many steps. Users may feel the task is longer than it should be.
aliases: long form| form friction| excessive fields| tedious input
examples: I had to enter the same address twice during checkout.

name: Unclear Form Requirements
description: Users do not know what information is required, what format is expected, or why certain information is being requested. This often leads to failed submissions or hesitation.
aliases: unclear field| missing requirement| format confusion| input ambiguity
examples: The phone number field failed, but it never showed the required format.

name: Poor Search Experience
description: Search does not help users find relevant content efficiently. Results may be irrelevant, poorly ranked, hard to filter, or empty without useful suggestions.
aliases: bad search| irrelevant results| weak filtering| search friction
examples: I searched for invoice, but the billing page did not appear.

name: Ineffective Filtering or Sorting
description: Filters and sorting controls are difficult to understand, apply, combine, reset, or interpret. Users may not know whether filters are active or why results changed.
aliases: filter friction| sorting issue| hidden filters| unclear results
examples: I applied a filter but could not tell if it was active.

name: Loss of User Input
description: The system unexpectedly clears, resets, or loses information the user has entered. This can happen after navigation, errors, refreshes, session timeouts, or validation failures.
aliases: lost data| cleared form| lost progress| reset input
examples: After the page refreshed, everything I typed disappeared.

name: Unexpected State Change
description: The interface changes state, navigates away, refreshes, closes, expands, collapses, or modifies data without the user clearly initiating or expecting it.
aliases: surprising behavior| unexpected change| sudden reset| unpredictable state
examples: The page jumped back to the top after I selected one checkbox.

name: Poor Onboarding
description: New users are not given enough guidance to understand the product, complete first-time tasks, or learn key concepts. Guidance may be missing, excessive, poorly timed, or not actionable.
aliases: weak onboarding| poor first-time use| lack of guidance| confusing start
examples: I landed on the dashboard but had no idea what to do first.

name: Poor Learnability
description: Users struggle to understand how to use the interface even after exploring it. Controls, flows, terminology, and system behavior do not teach themselves clearly through design.
aliases: hard to learn| steep learning curve| confusing first use| unintuitive UI
examples: I had to click around randomly to understand how the feature worked.

name: Poor Memorability
description: Users who return after time away cannot easily remember how to perform tasks. The interface depends too much on recall instead of recognition, or uses inconsistent paths and labels.
aliases: hard to remember| recall burden| forgettable workflow| low recognizability
examples: I used this last week but could not remember where the export option was.

name: Inefficient Workflow
description: A task requires more steps, clicks, screens, or manual effort than necessary. Users can complete the task, but the process feels slower or more cumbersome than expected.
aliases: too many steps| inefficient flow| excessive clicks| slow workflow
examples: To update one setting, I had to go through four different screens.

name: Redundant Actions
description: Users are asked to repeat actions, confirmations, entries, selections, or decisions that the system should remember or infer. This creates unnecessary friction and frustration.
aliases: repetition| duplicate effort| repeated input| redundant step
examples: Every time I opened the page, I had to select the same preferences again.

name: Poor Default Values
description: The interface provides defaults that are unhelpful, risky, confusing, or poorly matched to common user needs. Users must correct the system before continuing.
aliases: bad defaults| wrong preset| unsafe default| poor preselection
examples: The form defaulted to public visibility, but I expected private.

name: Unclear System Status
description: Users cannot tell what mode, step, state, selection, progress, or condition the system is currently in. This leads to hesitation and mistakes.
aliases: unclear status| missing state| no progress indicator| state confusion
examples: I could not tell whether the document was still a draft or already published.

name: Missing Progress Indicator
description: Users do not know how many steps are involved, where they are in a process, or how much remains. This makes multi-step workflows feel uncertain or longer than they are.
aliases: no progress| unclear steps| missing stepper| process uncertainty
examples: During setup, I had no idea whether I was on step two or step ten.

name: Confirmation Overload
description: The interface asks for confirmation too often or in low-risk situations, interrupting the user’s flow and reducing efficiency. Important confirmations may become easier to ignore.
aliases: too many prompts| modal fatigue| unnecessary confirmation| interruptive dialog
examples: It asked me to confirm every small change, which slowed me down.

name: Insufficient Confirmation for Destructive Action
description: The interface does not clearly warn users before actions that delete, overwrite, cancel, publish, charge, or otherwise cause significant consequences.
aliases: dangerous action| weak warning| accidental deletion| destructive action issue
examples: I deleted the project without realizing there would be no undo.

name: Poor Undo Support
description: Users cannot easily reverse actions, recover from mistakes, or restore previous states. This increases anxiety and discourages exploration.
aliases: no undo| irreversible action| poor recovery| restore issue
examples: I archived the item by mistake and could not find a way to undo it.

name: Misleading Affordance
description: An element looks interactive when it is not, or does not look interactive when it is. Users misunderstand what can be clicked, dragged, expanded, edited, or selected.
aliases: false affordance| unclear clickability| misleading control| hidden interaction
examples: The heading looked like a button, but clicking it did nothing.

name: Icon Ambiguity
description: Icons are difficult to interpret without labels, tooltips, or context. Users may guess incorrectly or avoid using the control altogether.
aliases: unclear icon| confusing symbol| icon-only issue| ambiguous control
examples: I did not know whether the icon meant share, upload, or send.

name: Poor Help and Documentation
description: Users cannot find useful assistance when they need it, or the available help is too generic, outdated, hidden, or disconnected from the task context.
aliases: weak help| poor documentation| missing guidance| unhelpful support
examples: The help article explained the old interface, not the screen I was using.

name: Overuse of Jargon
description: The interface uses technical, internal, legal, or domain-specific language that users do not understand. This creates barriers to learning and task completion.
aliases: technical language| confusing terminology| internal terms| jargon-heavy
examples: I did not know what provisioning a workspace meant.

name: Poor Personalization Control
description: Users cannot easily adjust settings, preferences, notifications, privacy, layout, or other experience parameters that affect their use. Controls may be hidden, limited, or hard to understand.
aliases: settings friction| poor preferences| limited control| customization issue
examples: I wanted fewer notifications but could not find the setting.

name: Intrusive Interruption
description: Popups, banners, modals, surveys, ads, or permission prompts interrupt users at the wrong time or block important tasks. This damages satisfaction and task flow.
aliases: interruptive modal| annoying popup| intrusive prompt| flow interruption
examples: A newsletter popup covered the form before I could finish reading it.

name: Trust or Credibility Issue
description: The interface makes users doubt whether the service is reliable, safe, current, or legitimate. This can result from inconsistent design, missing details, unclear policies, broken links, or suspicious requests.
aliases: low trust| credibility problem| suspicious UI| confidence issue
examples: The payment page looked different from the rest of the site, so I hesitated.

name: Privacy Control Confusion
description: Users cannot understand or confidently manage what information is shared, visible, stored, tracked, or used. Privacy settings may be hidden, vague, or overly complex.
aliases: privacy friction| unclear visibility| data control issue| sharing confusion
examples: I could not tell who would be able to see my profile information.

name: Notification Overload
description: The system sends too many notifications, poorly timed notifications, or notifications that are not useful. Users may ignore important alerts or disable notifications entirely.
aliases: too many alerts| notification fatigue| noisy notifications| irrelevant alerts
examples: I received several emails for the same update.

name: Poor Empty State
description: A screen with no content does not explain what happened, what the user can do next, or how to create or find content. Empty states become dead ends instead of useful guidance.
aliases: empty screen| dead end| no results guidance| blank state
examples: The page just said No items, but did not tell me how to add one.

name: Poor No-Results Handling
description: When search or filtering returns no results, the interface does not help users recover. It may fail to suggest alternatives, spelling corrections, filter resets, or broader queries.
aliases: no results issue| empty results| search dead end| filter dead end
examples: After filtering, I got no results and no option to clear all filters.

name: Content Not Scannable
description: Users struggle to quickly identify relevant information because content lacks headings, summaries, bullets, grouping, emphasis, or meaningful ordering.
aliases: hard to scan| poor content structure| dense content| weak chunking
examples: I had to read every paragraph to find the delivery date.

name: Poor Data Display
description: Tables, charts, metrics, lists, or cards present data in a way that is hard to compare, interpret, sort, or act on. Important values may lack context, labels, units, or explanation.
aliases: confusing data| unclear metrics| poor table| hard comparison
examples: The dashboard showed a score but did not explain whether it was good or bad.

name: Action Placement Issue
description: Controls are placed far from the content they affect, in unexpected locations, or inconsistently across screens. Users may miss actions or apply them to the wrong object.
aliases: bad button placement| misplaced action| detached control| action confusion
examples: I clicked Delete thinking it applied to one item, but it deleted the whole group.

name: Mode Confusion
description: Users do not realize they are in a specific mode such as edit, preview, selection, admin, private, public, draft, or published. Actions may behave differently depending on the mode.
aliases: unclear mode| edit confusion| selection mode issue| context confusion
examples: I thought I was editing the live page, but I was only changing a draft.

name: Poor Internationalization or Localization
description: The interface does not adapt properly to users’ language, region, date format, currency, address format, reading direction, or cultural expectations. This can cause misunderstanding or failed input.
aliases: localization issue| region mismatch| format issue| translation problem
examples: The date 06/11 was ambiguous and I was not sure which month it meant.

name: Broken Link or Dead End
description: A link, button, navigation path, or workflow leads to an error, unavailable page, irrelevant destination, or place with no useful next step. This blocks progress and damages trust.
aliases: dead link| broken path| navigation dead end| missing destination
examples: The Help link opened a 404 page.

name: Session Timeout Friction
description: The user is logged out or loses access unexpectedly, especially during a task. The interface does not warn them, preserve work, or help them resume smoothly.
aliases: timeout issue| unexpected logout| expired session| session loss
examples: I was logged out while writing the form and lost everything.

name: Permission or Access Confusion
description: Users cannot understand why they can or cannot access something, what permission is needed, or how to request access. The system may block users without explanation.
aliases: access issue| permission confusion| blocked action| role confusion
examples: The button was disabled, but it did not say what permission I needed.

name: Poor Satisfaction or Emotional Friction
description: The interface technically works but creates irritation, anxiety, boredom, distrust, or lack of confidence. This may result from tone, pacing, visual design, interruptions, unclear progress, or repeated small frustrations.
aliases: frustrating experience| low satisfaction| emotional friction| unpleasant UX
examples: I completed the task, but the process felt annoying and stressful.

name: Feature Discoverability Issue
description: A useful feature exists but users do not notice it, understand that it is available, or know when to use it. The feature may be hidden in menus, poorly labeled, or weakly introduced.
aliases: hidden feature| low discoverability| hard to find| feature invisibility
examples: I did not realize there was a bulk edit option until someone showed me.

name: Poor Comparison Support
description: Users cannot easily compare products, plans, options, results, or settings because relevant information is scattered, incomplete, or presented inconsistently.
aliases: hard comparison| comparison friction| option confusion| decision support issue
examples: I had to open each plan in a separate tab to compare the features.

name: Decision Paralysis
description: The interface presents too many similar options or insufficient guidance for choosing between them. Users delay or avoid action because the decision feels unclear.
aliases: too many choices| choice overload| unclear decision| option overload
examples: There were five subscription options and I could not tell which one I needed.
